tracks.title: Digital Foundations
tracks.description: Build essential digital skills: open-source first, internet-safe, no prior experience required.

tracks.title: Productivity
tracks.description: Master modern personal productivity, focus, and knowledge work with proven open-source tools.

tracks.title: Collaboration
tracks.description: Work, communicate, and ship together: privacy-respecting, self-hostable team workflows.

tracks.title: Creativity
tracks.description: Design, draw, animate, edit, and publish: professional-grade tools for every creative discipline.

tracks.title: Specialized Skills
tracks.description: Role-specific pathways for researchers, developers, accountants, and educators.

toolkits.title: Digital Foundations
toolkits.tagline: Your first confident steps online: safe, private, and free.
toolkits.description: A welcoming starting point for anyone new to digital tools. Learn to browse safely, communicate privately, manage files, and protect your accounts. No jargon, no cost.
outcomes: Browse the internet safely with privacy-respecting tools
Send secure messages and email to family, friends, and colleagues
Protect your passwords, files, and personal data

stages.title: Browse Safely & Privately
stages.description: Start with a safer browser and learn the basics of staying private online, your foundation for everything else.
objectives: Choose a privacy-respecting browser as your daily default
Recognize trackers, phishing, and unsafe sites
Set up a private alternative for sensitive browsing
tasks: Install Firefox or LibreWolf and import your bookmarks
Try a private browsing window for one full day
Switch your default search engine to a private option

stages.title: Communicate Securely
stages.description: Replace insecure SMS and unencrypted email with private, end-to-end encrypted alternatives.
objectives: Send your first end-to-end encrypted message
Set up a private email account
Verify a contact's identity for confidential conversations
tasks: Install Signal and invite one trusted contact
Create a Tutanota or ProtonMail account for private email
Try Element for an encrypted group chat

stages.title: Protect Passwords & Files
stages.description: Stop reusing passwords. Start backing up what matters. Two habits that change everything.
objectives: Move every account into a password manager
Generate unique strong passwords for your top 10 sites
Establish a simple, automatic file backup routine
tasks: Set up Bitwarden or KeePassXC and import your saved passwords
Replace passwords on your 5 most important accounts
Sync one important folder with Syncthing or Nextcloud

stages.title: Read, Watch & Listen
stages.description: Free, ad-free media tools for everyday digital life: documents, video, and audio.
objectives: Open and edit any document format without paying
Play any audio or video file reliably
Read PDFs and ebooks comfortably
tasks: Install LibreOffice and open one document, spreadsheet, and slide deck
Set VLC as your default media player
Open a PDF in Okular and try its annotation tools

toolkits.title: Research Starter Kit
toolkits.tagline: Capture, cite, and publish: the open-source research stack.
toolkits.description: Essential tools for students and academics beginning their research journey, from note-taking to citation management to academic writing.
outcomes: Build a connected, searchable personal knowledge base
Manage citations and bibliographies without manual formatting
Draft and publish academic papers in any format

stages.title: Capture & Organize Notes
stages.description: Start by building a personal knowledge base. These tools help you capture ideas, web clips, and research notes.
objectives: Adopt a daily-notes workflow that fits your style
Capture web articles and PDFs into your library
Connect notes with bidirectional links to surface insight
tasks: Pick one tool from this stage and create your first daily note
Clip 3 web pages and tag them by topic
Connect 2 notes using a backlink

stages.title: Manage References & Citations
stages.description: Keep your bibliography organized. These tools handle citations, PDFs, and reference lists for academic writing.
objectives: Build a reference library you can search and cite from
Use citation styles (APA, MLA, Chicago) without manual formatting
Sync references across devices and writing tools
tasks: Import 5 PDFs into Zotero or JabRef
Generate a bibliography in your preferred citation style
Install the browser connector and clip one paper directly from the web

stages.title: Write & Publish
stages.description: Draft papers and reports with tools built for academic and long-form writing.
objectives: Choose a writing tool that supports your output format
Convert between Markdown, LaTeX, DOCX, and PDF cleanly
Maintain focus during long writing sessions
tasks: Draft a 500-word section in LibreOffice or LyX
Use Pandoc to convert one Markdown file to PDF
Try FocusWriter for a 25-minute distraction-free session

toolkits.title: Student Productivity Pack
toolkits.tagline: Stay organized. Study smarter. Submit on time.
toolkits.description: A curated set of tools to help students stay organized, collaborate on projects, and get more done every day.
outcomes: Keep notes, tasks, and deadlines under control across every subject
Collaborate on group projects without paid software
Visualize complex topics to study and present better

stages.title: Notes & Task Management
stages.description: Build good study habits with note-taking apps and task managers that keep your workload under control.
objectives: Capture every class, assignment, and idea in one place
Plan your week using a simple kanban or calendar
Build a spaced-repetition habit for memorization
tasks: Take notes in Joplin or AppFlowy for one full class day
Set up a Focalboard with three columns: To Do · Doing · Done
Create your first 10 Anki cards from this week's lessons

stages.title: Documents & Collaboration
stages.description: Create, edit, and share documents with classmates using these office and collaboration tools.
objectives: Edit any document format without paying for software
Co-write a document live with classmates
Share notes securely without sign-up friction
tasks: Write a paper in LibreOffice and export it to PDF
Open a CryptPad doc and invite a classmate to edit live
Try HedgeDoc for a real-time Markdown study group session

stages.title: Diagrams & Visual Thinking
stages.description: Visualize concepts, plan projects, and brainstorm ideas with diagramming and mind-mapping tools.
objectives: Turn complex topics into visual study aids
Map your project ideas before you start writing
Communicate concepts clearly in presentations
tasks: Draw a mind map of one chapter using Freeplane or XMind
Build a flowchart in draw.io for a process you're studying
Document a system using Mermaid syntax

toolkits.title: Teacher's Digital Classroom
toolkits.tagline: Build engaging lessons. Reach every learner.
toolkits.description: Tools to help educators create engaging lessons, manage content, and support students in digital and hybrid classrooms.
outcomes: Author interactive lessons and learning content
Run a hybrid classroom with privacy-respecting tools
Assess student progress with structured feedback

stages.title: Create Learning Content
stages.description: Build interactive lessons, presentations, and educational materials your students will actually enjoy.
objectives: Author a multi-format lesson (slides, handouts, quizzes)
Create one interactive learning experience
Publish materials in a format learners can access offline
tasks: Build a slide deck and matching handout in LibreOffice
Try one H5P interaction (drag-the-words or quiz)
Package a Kolibri channel of your favorite resources

stages.title: Classroom & Communication Tools
stages.description: Manage your classroom, communicate with students, and share resources efficiently.
objectives: Run a class discussion in a private, ad-free space
Share resources without forcing sign-ups
Co-author class notes with students in real time
tasks: Create a Canvas LMS course shell for one unit
Run a 15-minute live note session in Etherpad
Publish a class wiki on BookStack

stages.title: Assessment & Feedback
stages.description: Create quizzes, track student progress, and provide structured feedback with these tools.
objectives: Author one formative and one summative assessment
Use spaced repetition for vocabulary or concept retention
Document a feedback workflow you can reuse every term
tasks: Build an Anki shared deck for your class
Try GCompris for a younger-learner activity
Document one assessment rubric in DokuWiki

toolkits.title: Remote Team Collaboration
toolkits.tagline: Work better together: privacy-respecting, self-hostable, free.
toolkits.description: A complete open-source collaboration stack for distributed teams: chat, video, shared docs, and file sync. Replace expensive SaaS with tools you control.
outcomes: Run a privacy-respecting team chat and video stack
Co-author documents and notes in real time without vendor lock-in
Sync and share files across your team securely

stages.title: Team Chat & Messaging
stages.description: Replace closed-source workplace chat with self-hostable, encryption-aware alternatives that respect your team's privacy.
objectives: Set up a team chat workspace with channels and DMs
Establish a messaging hygiene protocol (channels vs DMs)
Verify identity and end-to-end encryption is on
tasks: Create channels for #general, #random, and one project
Invite three teammates and pin a welcome message
Run a stand-up using threads or scheduled posts

stages.title: Video & Voice Meetings
stages.description: Host meetings without licenses, accounts, or attendee caps. Jitsi runs in the browser, no install.
objectives: Run a meeting with no install required for guests
Record and share a meeting summary
Set up a low-latency voice channel for daily work
tasks: Host a Jitsi call with two guests and screen-share
Try Mumble or TeamSpeak for an always-on voice room
Set a recurring weekly meeting room URL

stages.title: Shared Docs & Notes
stages.description: Co-author documents, take live meeting notes, and build a team knowledge base. No third-party account required.
objectives: Co-edit a document in real time with at least two teammates
Maintain meeting notes the team can search later
Publish a public-facing knowledge base
tasks: Co-write a one-page proposal in CryptPad
Run a meeting with live notes in HedgeDoc or Etherpad
Spin up a BookStack knowledge base for your team

stages.title: File Sync & Sharing
stages.description: Self-hostable file-sharing: your data, your storage, your control.
objectives: Sync a shared team folder across devices
Share a file via expiring, password-protected link
Establish one place for all team files
tasks: Set up Nextcloud or Seafile and sync a team folder
Create one share link with an expiry date
Mirror a critical folder with Syncthing for offline-first work

toolkits.title: Workplace Productivity for Professionals
toolkits.tagline: A professional-grade open-source stack for daily work.
toolkits.description: For working professionals who want to do their best work without subscription fatigue: office, knowledge, automation, and security tools that feel premium.
outcomes: Replace your office suite with a professional open-source equivalent
Build a personal knowledge system that compounds over time
Lock down your accounts and data with industry-standard tools

stages.title: Office & Documents
stages.description: A complete office suite that opens, edits, and exports every common format, desktop or browser.
objectives: Edit DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX without compatibility issues
Pick a primary office tool and stick with it for 7 days
Set up a clean PDF reading and annotation workflow
tasks: Open three real work documents in LibreOffice or OnlyOffice
Annotate one PDF in Okular and email it back
Export one document to PDF/A for archiving

stages.title: Personal Knowledge System
stages.description: A second brain for projects, meeting notes, and references: searchable, linked, and yours forever.
objectives: Capture meeting notes with consistent structure
Link related notes to surface patterns
Establish a weekly review ritual
tasks: Create a daily-notes template in Obsidian or Logseq
Connect 5 notes with backlinks
Schedule a 15-minute Friday review on your calendar

stages.title: Security & Privacy Stack
stages.description: Industry-standard password management, encryption, and private communication for working professionals.
objectives: Move every work account into a password manager
Use end-to-end encrypted email for sensitive threads
Verify two-factor authentication on critical accounts
tasks: Audit and replace 10 reused passwords in Bitwarden
Send one E2EE email via ProtonMail or Tutanota
Set up Signal as a secondary work-comms channel

stages.title: Automation & Backup
stages.description: Stop losing work. Stop doing the same task twice. The professional's safety net.
objectives: Establish an automatic backup of your critical files
Sync work data across devices reliably
Document one repeatable workflow you can hand off
tasks: Set up a daily Restic or Borg backup of one folder
Sync your laptop and desktop with Syncthing
Mirror a folder to an external drive with rclone

toolkits.title: Self-Directed Learner's Toolkit
toolkits.tagline: Learn anything, retain it, build something.
toolkits.description: For lifelong learners building their own curriculum. A structured stack for memorization, deep reading, hands-on practice, and turning what you learn into work you ship.
outcomes: Build a memorization habit that survives months, not days
Read deeply and capture insights you'll actually revisit
Turn your learning into a portfolio you can show

stages.title: Memorize What Matters
stages.description: Spaced repetition is the closest thing to a learning superpower. Make it a 5-minute daily habit.
objectives: Build a daily 5-minute review habit
Author 20 cards on your current topic
Use cloze deletion for nuanced concepts
tasks: Install Anki and pick one shared deck to review daily for a week
Author 20 of your own cards from your current subject
Schedule a daily 5-minute review on your calendar

stages.title: Read & Capture Deeply
stages.description: Go beyond highlighting. Capture, link, and revisit what you read so it shapes how you think.
objectives: Set up a reading queue you'll actually finish
Capture book and article notes in a searchable system
Link new ideas to what you already know
tasks: Import 3 ebooks into Calibre and start a reading queue
Take notes on one article in Obsidian or Logseq
Connect today's notes to two older notes

stages.title: Practice in Public
stages.description: Build something small with what you learn. Public practice compounds faster than private study.
objectives: Pick a small build project tied to your current learning
Use a notebook or sandbox to experiment freely
Publish or share one artifact this week
tasks: Open a Jupyter notebook and run your first cell
Try one of: a script, a sketch, a writeup, or a short demo
Post or share one result with a friend or community

toolkits.title: Beginner Coding Path
toolkits.tagline: From your first line of code to your first pull request.
toolkits.description: Start your programming journey with the right tools, from writing your first lines of code to version control basics and hands-on AI experimentation.
outcomes: Write, run, and debug code in a modern editor
Track your work and collaborate using Git
Experiment with AI and notebooks to learn faster

stages.title: Pick Your Editor
stages.description: Choose a code editor that fits your style. These are beginner-friendly options to get you writing code fast.
objectives: Pick one editor and customize it lightly
Install one language extension you'll use
Build muscle memory for save, run, and find
tasks: Install VS Code or Kate and write a Hello World
Install one extension for the language you're learning
Practice three keyboard shortcuts until they're automatic

stages.title: Version Control Basics
stages.description: Learn to track your code changes and collaborate with others using Git-based tools.
objectives: Initialize a repo and make commits with meaningful messages
Push your code to a remote you control
Open and merge your first pull request
tasks: Create a Git repo for one small personal project
Push it to Gitea or Forgejo
Open one pull request and merge it

stages.title: Interactive Learning & Notebooks
stages.description: Experiment with code in interactive environments, great for learning Python, data science, and scripting.
objectives: Run code in a notebook and chart one dataset
Try local AI to learn without paying per token
Build a tiny end-to-end script from scratch
tasks: Open Jupyter and run your first 10 cells
Try Ollama with one local model and ask it three questions
Write a 20-line script that solves a real annoyance

toolkits.title: Designer's Toolkit
toolkits.tagline: Pixels, vectors, type, and motion: all open-source.
toolkits.description: A complete open-source design workflow, from raster and vector editing to UI prototyping, typography, and print-ready layouts.
outcomes: Run a full creative workflow without proprietary software
Ship raster, vector, UI, print, and motion deliverables
Build a portfolio piece using only FOSS tools

stages.title: Raster & Vector Editing
stages.description: Master the foundational tools for editing photos and creating scalable vector graphics.
objectives: Edit a photo with non-destructive layers
Draw a vector logo in Inkscape from scratch
Export at the right size for web, print, and social
tasks: Edit one photo in GIMP using layers and masks
Draw a simple logo in Inkscape and export as SVG and PNG
Try Krita for a quick digital sketch

stages.title: UI Design & Prototyping
stages.description: Design interfaces and interactive prototypes with tools built for modern product design workflows.
objectives: Design a one-screen UI with consistent components
Build an interactive prototype with at least two states
Hand off specs and assets cleanly
tasks: Design a sign-in screen in Penpot using auto-layout
Build a clickable two-screen prototype
Export design tokens and assets for development

stages.title: Typography & Print
stages.description: Create custom typefaces and produce professional print-ready layouts for publications and marketing materials.
objectives: Lay out a multi-page document with master pages
Choose and pair typefaces with intent
Export press-ready PDF/X for a print shop
tasks: Lay out a 4-page brochure in Scribus
Sketch one custom letterform in FontForge or BirdFont
Export a CMYK PDF/X-1a from Scribus

stages.title: Animation & Motion
stages.description: Bring your designs to life with 2D animation and motion graphics tools used by professionals worldwide.
objectives: Animate one short loop or a 5-second motion piece
Try keyframing and easing in a real timeline
Render and export at proper resolution and codec
tasks: Animate a 3-second logo reveal in Synfig or Pencil2D
Try a simple bouncing-ball exercise to learn easing
Render and share one short piece on social

toolkits.title: Accountant's Essentials
toolkits.tagline: Books, budgets, and BI: open-source from end to end.
toolkits.description: Open-source tools for bookkeeping, financial reporting, budgeting, and data analysis, built for accounting professionals.
outcomes: Maintain double-entry books for a small business or personal use
Build budgets and cash-flow forecasts you actually use
Turn raw financial data into dashboards stakeholders trust

stages.title: Bookkeeping & Accounting
stages.description: Record transactions, manage accounts, and produce financial statements with these double-entry accounting tools.
objectives: Set up a chart of accounts for one entity
Reconcile one bank statement end-to-end
Produce a P&L and balance sheet for a single period
tasks: Create a sample company in GnuCash and enter 10 transactions
Reconcile last month's bank statement
Generate a P&L for a single period

stages.title: Budgeting & Personal Finance
stages.description: Track budgets, forecast cash flow, and manage personal or small-business finances with clarity.
objectives: Build an envelope or zero-based budget
Forecast cash flow for the next 3 months
Set up category-level reporting you can review weekly
tasks: Build a category budget in Firefly III or Actual
Import 30 days of transactions and categorize them
Set a 15-minute weekly money-review on your calendar

stages.title: Reporting & Data Analysis
stages.description: Turn raw financial data into actionable insights with BI dashboards, SQL tools, and spreadsheet analysis.
objectives: Connect a database or CSV to a BI tool
Build one shareable dashboard
Clean a messy dataset before analysis
tasks: Stand up Metabase against a sample finance dataset
Build a 3-card dashboard (revenue, expenses, margin)
Clean one CSV with OpenRefine

stages.title: Data & Spreadsheet Tools
stages.description: Work with structured data, clean datasets, and run statistical analysis to support financial decision-making.
objectives: Query a database without writing wall-of-SQL
Run a basic statistical analysis on a real dataset
Publish a reproducible analysis you can rerun next month
tasks: Connect DBeaver to a sample database and run 3 queries
Run a basic regression in R-Project or a notebook
Publish a Datasette of one cleaned dataset
